You extract source evidence for a paper-derived scientific benchmark. Return exactly one JSON object matching the supplied schema, with no Markdown or additional text.

Use only the fixed, line-numbered source packet. Do not use outside knowledge and do not infer an omitted coefficient, exponent, range, experimental condition, or uncertainty convention.

Extract at most one relation: the best source-supported executable quantitative relation connecting one to five numeric controls to one or two numeric readouts. A second source-reported condition is not required. Do not construct a pair, alternate world, counterfactual, task prompt, or benchmark design. If the source contains no complete relation, return {"relations":[]}.

The relation has exactly six fields: formula, parameters, controls, readouts, domain, and anchors. Formula.outputs is an executable expression tree for the source-reported central relation. Output keys must exactly match the readout names. A var leaf names a declared control and a param leaf names a declared parameter. Every declared control and parameter must occur in the formula. Numeric literals are allowed only for structural zero and one; encode every other scientific constant or fitted value as an anchored parameter. Preserve equality, approximation, fitted-relation, and asymptotic scope through the applicability statements; do not turn proportionality without its coefficient, an inequality, or an unspecified function into an exact point predictor.

A control is a numeric independent variable that can be queried within the source-supported domain. A readout is the quantitative dependent variable returned by the relation. Do not turn a latent quantity or an unreported fitted quantity into a control. Use continuous_interval only when the source supports a finite interval with minimum below maximum. Use numeric_values only for at least two explicitly supported numeric values. The domain must name every control exactly once. Record source-reported applicability or fixed context when present; otherwise use an empty applicability array.

Every formula, parameter value, control definition, readout definition, control domain, and applicability statement must carry direct inclusive source line ranges. Anchors contain line_start and line_end only. Do not generate a paraphrased support field. Use the line coordinates exactly as supplied.

Do not output source identity, schema version, an assessment, readiness flag, mechanisms, claim dependencies, ambiguity records, budget, diagnostic conditions, held-out conditions, public prose, provenance mappings, or code. Source identity and all benchmark-design fields are supplied or generated by deterministic code.

L000051	
L000052	\preprint{CERN-TH-2026-019, ZU-TH 03/26}
L000053	
L000054	\title{\boldmath Precise QCD Predictions for Hadron-in-jet Production in \texorpdfstring{$e^+e^-$}{e+e-} Collisions}
L000055	
L000056	\author{Leonardo Bonino$^a$, Aude Gehrmann-De Ridder$^{a,b}$,\\ Thomas Gehrmann$^a$,
L000057	Alexander Huss$^c$, Francesco Merlotti$^b$, Giovanni Stagnitto$^d$}
L000058	\affiliation{$^a$
L000059	  Physik-Institut, Universit\"at Z\"urich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, 8057 Z\"urich, Switzerland\\
L000060	$^b$
L000061	   Institute for Theoretical Physics, ETH, CH-8093 Zürich, Switzerland\\
L000062	   $^c$  Theoretical Physics Department, CERN, 1211 Geneva 23, Switzerland\\
L000063	$^d$  Universit\`{a} di Genova \& INFN, Via Dodecaneso 33, I-16146 Genova, Italy}
L000064	
L000065	\begin{abstract}
L000066	The production of identified hadrons inside jets in $e^+ e^-$ annihilation allows for detailed studies of parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions in a clean environment.
L000067	We compute hadron-in-jets production cross sections for $e^+e^- \to 2\,\mathrm{jets}$ and $e^+e^- \to 3\,\mathrm{jets}$ to next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in perturbative QCD. By comparing with data from the ALEPH experiment, we demonstrate the implications of the newly computed theory predictions for precision phenomenology.
L000068	\end{abstract}
L000069	
L000070	\maketitle
L000071	
L000072	\textit{Introduction---}\ignorespaces
L000073	Studying identified hadrons inside jets provides valuable insights into jet formation, its partonic composition, and on the parton-to-hadron fragmentation~\cite{Procura:2009vm,Jain:2011xz,Kaufmann:2015hma}.
L000074	These studies are best performed in the clean environment of $e^+e^-$ annihilation.
L000075	The LEP experiments provided a substantial amount of precision measurements of identified-hadron production cross sections.
L000076	These data have been instrumental in the tuning of hadronization models in multi-purpose event simulation programs.
L000077	For these data to be equally relevant to precision QCD studies, theory predictions that allow to describe the full kinematics of the final state containing the identified hadron are required.
L000078	
L000079	Precision calculations for identified hadron cross sections have been performed up to now solely for semi-inclusive observables in $e^+e^-$ annihilation (SIA), which are differential only in the energy fraction of the identified hadron in the event, but fully inclusive on the rest of the final state.
L000080	For SIA, QCD corrections up to third order in perturbation theory (N\textsuperscript{3}LO) are known~\cite{Altarelli:1979kv,Rijken:1996vr,Rijken:1996ns,Mitov:2006ic,He:2025hin}.
L000081	These are routinely included in fits of parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions (FFs) for various hadron species at next-to-leading order (NLO)~\cite{Binnewies:1994ju,Binnewies:1995pt,Kniehl:2000fe,Bourhis:2000gs,Kretzer:2000yf,Kretzer:2001pz,deFlorian:2007ekg,deFlorian:2014xna,deFlorian:2017lwf,Borsa:2021ran,Hirai:2007cx,Albino:2008fy,Bertone:2018ecm,Khalek:2021gxf,Moffat:2021dji,Gao:2024dbv,Gao:2024nkz,Gao:2025bko} and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO)~\cite{Bertone:2017tyb,Anderle:2015lqa,Abdolmaleki:2021yjf,Borsa:2022vvp,Gao:2025hlm,AbdulKhalek:2022laj,Li:2024etc}.
L000082	These fits usually combine data on SIA, semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS), also known to NNLO~\cite{Altarelli:1979kv,deFlorian:1997zj,Bonino:2024qbh,Goyal:2023zdi}, and identified hadron production at hadron colliders.
L000083	Semi-inclusive coefficient functions for the latter are known to NLO~\cite{Aversa:1988vb,Jager:2002xm}, and fully differential cross sections at NNLO have been obtained most recently~\cite{Czakon:2025yti,Generet:2025bqx}.
L000084	
L000085	Future electron--positron colliders~\cite{FCC:2025lpp} will produce enormous data sets of hadronic final states, thereby allowing a new era of precision QCD studies~\cite{Zhou:2024cyk,dEnterria:2025pml}.
L000086	To enable these studies, theory predictions must go beyond the simple SIA kinematics and include full final state descriptions for identified hadron observables.
L000087	In this letter, we present the first NNLO QCD calculation for identified hadron observables in 2-jet and 3-jet final states in $e^+e^-$ annihilation.
L000088	We demonstrate the impact of these corrections through a precise phenomenological study of ALEPH data on neutral light mesons in jet final states, whilst comparing predictions obtained employing recent determinations of FFs.
L000089	\newline
L000090	
L000091	\textit{Methodology---}\ignorespaces
L000092	We consider the production of 2-jet and 3-jet final states at $e^+e^-$ colliders, with one of the jets containing
L000093	an identified hadron $H$:
L000094	\begin{align}\label{eq:proc}
L000095	  e^+e^-& \to \jet(H)+\jet
L000096	  \, , \nonumber \\
L000097	  e^+e^-& \to \jet(H)+\jet + \jet
L000098	  \, .
L000099	\end{align}
L000100	In the fully differential cross section for these processes,
L000101	\begin{align}\label{eq:xs}
L000102	\dd\sigma^H=\sum_p\dd\sigma^{p\to H} = \sum_p \int\dd z D^H_p(z,\mu_a^2)\dd \hat{\sigma}_p(z,\mu_a^2) \, ,
L000103	\end{align}
L000104	the fragmentation function $D_p^H$ encodes the probability for the transition of the parton $p$ into the identified hadron $H$.
L000105	Collinear factorization is performed at a fragmentation scale $\mu_a$.
L000106	The short-distance one-parton-identified cross section $\dd \hat{\sigma}_p$ admits a perturbative expansion in the renormalized strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$
L000107	\begin{align}
L000108	\dd \hat{\sigma}_p = \dd \hat{\sigma}^{\mathrm{LO}}_p+\left(\frac{\alpha_s}{2\pi}\right) \dd \hat{\sigma}^{\mathrm{NLO}}_p+\left(\frac{\alpha_s}{2\pi}\right)^2 \dd \hat{\sigma}^{\mathrm{NNLO}}_p+\ldots \, .
L000109	\end{align}
L000110	Beyond leading order (LO), individual real and virtual contributions to the short distance
L000111	cross section contain infrared divergences.
L000112	To deal with such divergences at intermediate steps of the calculation, we adopt the \textit{antenna subtraction method}~\cite{Gehrmann-DeRidder:2005btv,Currie:2013vh}.
L000113	In this method, with the introduction of subtraction terms, infrared divergences associated to single- and double-unresolved configurations in real radiation matrix elements are extracted and recombined with virtual and collinear factorization contributions.
L000114	The building blocks of the subtraction terms are antenna functions that encode all possible radiation patterns between a pair of hard radiating partons.
L000115	
L000116	Since the fragmentation process is sensitive to the momentum fraction of individual partons within a collinear cluster, the identification of a parton in \eqref{eq:xs} affects the cancellation of collinear divergences.
L000117	The antenna subtraction method has been extended to account for identified hadrons as described in~\cite{Gehrmann:2022cih,Gehrmann:2022pzd,Bonino:2024adk}.
L000118	This extended formalism was first employed in the computation of charged hadrons inside jets in association with a leptonically decaying $Z$ boson at the LHC~\cite{Caletti:2024xaw}.
L000119	
L000120	In this work, we implement identified-hadron production for $e^+e^- \to 2\,\mathrm{jets}$ and $e^+e^- \to 3\,\mathrm{jets}$ processes through NNLO accuracy within the parton-level event generator \NNLOJET~\cite{NNLOJET:2025rno}.
L000121	The subtraction terms for these processes structurally resemble the ones for jet production in deep-inelastic scattering (DIS)~\cite{Currie:2017tpe}: initial-state collinear singularities in DIS are related to final-state collinear singularities in identified hadron production through crossing symmetry of matrix elements and subtraction terms.
L000122	
L000123	Identified hadron production in $e^+e^- \to 2\,\mathrm{jets}$ is validated against an implementation~\cite{Bonino:2023icn} of the NNLO coefficient functions~\cite{Rijken:1996vr,Rijken:1996ns,Mitov:2006ic} for SIA, where the convolution of coefficient functions and fragmentation functions is performed analytically in Mellin space.
L000124	\newline
L000125	
L000126	\textit{Phenomenological Setup---}\ignorespaces
L000127	The bulk of LEP data with identified hadrons in the final state are for SIA reactions, whereas only a limited set of measurements are available for hadron-in-jet production~\cite{ALEPH:1999udi,L3:1995rnv,OPAL:2004prv}.
L000128	
L000129	The ALEPH collaboration measured the production of identified neutral light hadrons ($\pi^0$ and $\eta$ mesons) in jet events~\cite{ALEPH:1999udi}, based on data collected at the $Z$ peak ($\sqrt{s}= M_Z = 91.2$ GeV).
L000130	Measured cross sections are presented differential in the observable
L000131	\begin{align}\label{eq:x}
L000132	x = \frac{2 E_H}{\sqrt{s}} \, ,
L000133	\end{align}
L000134	where $E_H$ is the energy of the identified hadron.
L000135	The differential cross sections are normalized to the fiducial cross section $\sigma_{\njets}$ for the production of $\njets$ jets.
L000136	
L000137	Jets are reconstructed from event tracks using the Durham jet algorithm~\cite{Catani:1991hj} with $\ycut = 0.01$.
L000138	In the study on hadron production in 3-jet events, jets are ordered according to their energy, providing distributions in $x$ for the leading (LJ), sub-leading (SLJ), and sub-sub-leading jet (SSLJ).
L000139	Events are accepted for $\theta_T\in \left[30^\circ,150^\circ\right]$ where $\theta_T$ is the polar angle between the thrust direction and the beam axis.
L000140	Jets are required to have a polar angle between the jet and the beam axis $\theta_j \in \left[30^\circ,150^\circ\right]$.
L000141	These criteria define fiducial cross sections for a given jet multiplicity.
L000142	In their analysis~\cite{ALEPH:1999udi}, the ALEPH collaboration corrected the data to full $4\pi$ solid angle acceptance using parton-shower event simulations.
L000143	
L000144	To demonstrate the feasibility of a data--theory comparison at fiducial cross section level, we recompute the
L000145	acceptance correction factors with \JETSET~\cite{Sjostrand:1994kzr} in analogy to the prescription in the ALEPH analysis.
L000146	We then use these correction factors to revert the data to fiducial cross section level.
L000147	Correction factors are between $0.95$ and $1.02$ for 2-jet $\pi^0$ data, $0.93$ and $0.99$ for 2-jet $\eta$ data, and between $0.96$ and $1.00$ for 3-jet $\pi^0$ data. In general, they exhibit only a moderate $x$ dependence.
L000148	In the phenomenological analysis that follows, all data are corrected with these acceptance factors.
L000149	
L000150	We present the first NNLO QCD predictions for the observables measured in~\cite{ALEPH:1999udi}.
L000151	The choice of renormalization and fragmentation scales deserve particular attention.
L000152	For the renormalization scale $\mu_r$ we adopt $\mu_r = \sqrt{s}$, as the hard scale of the overall process, and use $\alpha_s(M_Z)=0.118$.
L000153	Regarding the fragmentation scale $\mu_a$, in semi-inclusive calculations the only natural choice is $\sqrt{s}$.
L000154	In contrast, when hadrons are identified within jets, the maximum size of the jet $\ycut$ introduces an intrinsic cut-off for extra radiation, thereby reducing the fragmentation scale~\cite{Dokshitzer:1987nm,Dokshitzer:1991wu,Procura:2009vm,Jain:2011xz,Kaufmann:2015hma}.
L000155	We shall examine different choices of fragmentation scales in our QCD predictions.
L000156	
L000157	We investigate the impact of the FF sets used in predictions for 2-jet and 3-jet events for $\pi^0$ production by comparing four different FF sets from the BDSSV and the NPC collaborations: \BDSS~\cite{Borsa:2021ran}, \BDSSV~\cite{Borsa:2022vvp}, \NPCnlo~\cite{Gao:2025bko}, and \NPCnnlo~\cite{Gao:2025hlm}.
L000158	Both collaborations provide a NNLO set fitted to SIA and SIDIS data, and a NLO set with an improved description of $D_g^{\pi^0}$ due to the inclusion of proton--proton collision data in the fit.
L000159	For 2-jet events, we also focus on $\eta$ meson production and compared the results using the NLO FF sets \ALMSS~\cite{Aidala:2025kep} and \NPCeta~\cite{Gao:2025bko}.
L000160	\newline
L000161	
L000162	\begin{figure}[ht]
L000163	\centering
L000164	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig1.pdf}
L000165	\caption{Data--theory comparison for $\pi^0$ production in 2-jet exclusive events up NNLO with \BDSSV. Left panel: $\mu_a = \sqrt{s}$. Right panel: $\mu_a = \sqrt{\ycut s}$.}
L000166	\label{fig:2j_pi0}
L000167	\end{figure}
L000168	\textit{2-jet Results---}\ignorespaces
L000169	In Fig.~\ref{fig:2j_pi0} we compare our theoretical calculation to ALEPH data for $\pi^0$ production in 2-jet exclusive events.
L000170	Predictions up to NNLO are computed with the NNLO FF set \BDSSV.
L000171	Higher-order theory uncertainties, here and in what follows, are estimated with a 7-point scale variation of $\mu_r$ and $\mu_a$ around the central scales.
L000172	We investigate the effect of the fragmentation scale choice by comparing our predictions for two values of the central scale, $\mu_a=\sqrt{s}$ and $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$.
L000173	We observe that the perturbative convergence of the calculation drastically improves for $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$, with reduced perturbative corrections and good agreement between theory and data.
L000174	This observation confirms the assertion~\cite{Dokshitzer:1987nm,Dokshitzer:1991wu,Procura:2009vm,Jain:2011xz,Kaufmann:2015hma} that the typical hadron-in-jet production scale is determined by the individual jet kinematics rather than the full event kinematics.
L000175	
L000176	\begin{figure}[ht]
L000177	  \centering
L000178	  \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig2.pdf}
L000179	  \caption{Data--theory comparison of $\pi^0$ production in 2-jet exclusive events at NNLO with different FF sets.
L000180	  }
L000181	  \label{fig:2j_pi0_sets}
L000182	\end{figure}
L000183	
L000184	In Fig.~\ref{fig:2j_pi0_sets} we assess the performance of the NNLO predictions of $\pi^0$ 2-jet events computed with the selected FF sets.
L000185	We observe that the predictions are compatible within theoretical uncertainties for a given collaboration in the entire $x$ range, while for $x<0.32$ the predictions from BDSSV and NPC do not overlap.
L000186	The BDSSV FFs provide a better quantitative description of the data.
L000187	
L000188	
L000189	We find that the  dominant source of theoretical uncertainty comes from the variation of the fragmentation scale.
L000190	As previously observed in SIA~\cite{Rijken:1996vr,Rijken:1996ns}, the fragmentation-scale dependence of quark- and gluon-initiated contributions exhibits a partial cancellation at higher perturbative orders.
L000191	For $z<0.1$ at $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$, the
L000192	BDSSV sets differ considerably from the NPC sets. The sea-like shape of BDSSV  in this range
L000193	results in considerably larger absolute values of the quark and gluon induced contributions than the valence-like shape of NPC, leading to
L000194	larger scale-variation uncertainty bands in the differential distributions.
L000195	\begin{figure}[ht]
L000196	\centering
L000197	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig3.pdf}
L000198	\caption{Data--theory comparison for $\eta$ production in 2-jet exclusive events up NNLO for \ALMSS (green) and \NPCeta (purple) FF sets. Left panel: NLO. Right panel: NNLO.
L000199	}
L000200	\label{fig:2j_eta}
L000201	\end{figure}
L000202	
L000203	In Fig.~\ref{fig:2j_eta} we compare our theoretical predictions up to NNLO against ALEPH data for $\eta$ meson production in 2-jet exclusive events using the NLO FF sets \ALMSS and \NPCeta.
L000204	The $\eta$ data cover a larger kinematic range in $x$ as compared to the $\pi^0$ data.
L000205	Both sets provide a satisfactory description of the data for $0.2<x<0.7$.
L000206	While the \ALMSS provides a better description of the data at small $x$, the \NPCeta performs better at large $x$.
L000207	Overall, predictions computed with the \ALMSS FF set describe the data the best.
L000208	
L000209	As observed for $\pi^0$ 2-jet predictions, theoretical uncertainties are dominated by the fragmentation scale variation.
L000210	Predictions obtained with the \ALMSS set are more sensitive to $\mu_a$ variations as compared to the ones produced with \NPCeta.
L000211	
L000212	Accounting for FF uncertainties does not change the conclusions drawn above on the description of the data for both $\pi^0$ and $\eta$ in 2-jet observables.
L000213	Lastly, we note that none of the FF fits include the $\pi^0$ and $\eta$ 2-jet exclusive data.
L000214	\newline
L000215	
L000216	\begin{figure*}[t]
L000217	\centering
L000218	\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig4.pdf}
L000219	\caption{Data--theory comparison for $\pi^0$ production in 3-jet exclusive events up NNLO with \BDSSV. Left panel: $\mu_a = E_{j(H)}$. Right panel: $\mu_a = \sqrt{\ycut s}$.
L000220	}
L000221	\label{fig:3j_pi0_scales}
L000222	\end{figure*}
L000223	
L000224	\textit{3-jet Results---}\ignorespaces
L000225	Identified hadron production in 3-jet final states is particularly relevant due to its direct sensitivity
L000226	to the gluon-to-hadron FF.
L000227	
L000228	Similarly to the 2-jet observables, we investigate the effect of the choice of the fragmentation scale.
L000229	To produce predictions for 3-jet final states, we can choose between a jet resolution based scale $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$ and a jet energy based scale $\mu_a=E_{j(H)}$ corresponding to the energy of the jet containing the identified hadron.
L000230	In Fig.~\ref{fig:3j_pi0_scales} we compare our predictions up to NNLO computed with the \BDSSV FF set for the two choices of the fragmentation scale against $\pi^0$ 3-jet data.
L000231	Both fragmentation scale choices provide comparable predictions.
L000232	They yield an excellent description of the LJ data, which degrades consecutively for SLJ and SSLJ.
L000233	Predictions for both choices show good perturbative convergence, with $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$ featuring slightly smaller corrections and lower scale uncertainties.
L000234	
L000235	\begin{figure}[t]
L000236	\centering
L000237	\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig5.pdf}
L000238	\caption{Data--theory comparison of $\pi^0$ production in 3-jet exclusive events at NNLO with different FF sets.
L000239	}
L000240	\label{fig:3j_pi0_sets}
L000241	\end{figure}
L000242	
L000243	The \BDSSV set used in Fig.~\ref{fig:3j_pi0_scales} has been fitted only to SIA and SIDIS data, which are both largely dominated by quark fragmentation processes.
L000244	The resulting uncertainty on the gluon FF is the most likely explanation for the degrading description of the distributions in the SLJ and SSLJ.
L000245	To gain further insights into this matter, in Fig.~\ref{fig:3j_pi0_sets} we compare the NNLO predictions (for $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$) for the selected FF sets.
L000246	The LJ predominantly originates from quarks, and predictions for the LJ distribution with all FF sets describe the data equally well, reflecting the accuracy on the $D_q^{\pi^0}$ FFs.
L000247	The impact of gluon-initiated processes increases from LJ to SLJ and SSLJ.
L000248	Only the \BDSS and \NPCnlo sets include proton--proton collision data in their global fits, thereby providing more reliable constraints on the $D_g^{\pi^0}$ FF, which is reflected in better descriptions of the ALEPH data for the SLJ and SSLJ.
L000249	In particular the \NPCnlo set, which uses this specific dataset as a test observable, shows the best agreement with the data.
L000250	The improvement in the description of SLJ and SSLJ data confirms the relevance of the ALEPH data in constraining the gluon FF.
L000251	
L000252	As in the 2-jet analysis, the uncertainty from scale variations is predominantly driven by the fragmentation scale.
L000253	The larger overall uncertainty bands obtained with the BDSSV sets can be traced back to the small-$z$ behaviour of the corresponding fragmentation functions.
L000254	Unlike the 2-jet case, where the contribution of $D_g^{\pi^0}$ only plays a marginal role, the 3-jet observables show a stronger dependence on the FF uncertainties.
L000255	Nevertheless, these FF uncertainties do not alter the overall pattern of agreement among the different sets displayed in Fig.~\ref{fig:3j_pi0_sets}.
L000256	\newline
L000257	
L000258	\textit{On Gluon Fragmentation---}\ignorespaces
L000259	To illustrate the role of the gluon FF we perform a breakdown of the total fiducial 3-jet cross section into the $q$- and $g$-initiated fragmentation processes.
L000260	To this end, we define
L000261	\begin{align}
L000262	  R^{p \to \pi^0} = \frac{\sigma_3^{p \to \pi^0}}{\sigma_3^{\pi^0}}\, ,
L000263	\end{align}
L000264	as the ratio of fiducial cross sections for $\pi^0$ production in 3-jet events initiated through parton-type $p$ divided by the sum of all parton types.
L000265	In addition, to further investigate $\pi^0$ production separately for each jet of the 3-jet event, we introduce
L000266	\begin{align}
L000267	  R_{\jet}^{p \to \pi^0} = \frac{\sigma_{\jet}^{p \to \pi^0}}{\sigma_{\jet}^{\pi^0}}\, ,
L000268	\end{align}
L000269	where $\jet$ denotes the identification of the $\pi^0$ meson within the LJ, SLJ, or SSLJ.
L000270	
L000271	\input{tab1.tex}
L000272	
L000273	In Tab.~\ref{tab:id_parton_3jet} we report the values of $R^{p \to \pi^0}$ and $R_{\jet}^{p \to \pi^0}$ for $p=q,g$ up to NNLO for the \NPCnlo set and $\mu_a=\sqrt{\ycut s}$.
L000274	The fractions change only moderately with increasing perturbative orders, except for the SSLJ.
L000275	$\pi^0$ mesons in the LJ originate almost entirely from the fragmentation of a quark.
L000276	The contribution from gluons increases in the SLJ, with $g$-originated fragmentation accounting for 21\% of the events.
L000277	In the SSLJ, gluon fragmentation dominates the production of pions.
L000278	In this case, substantial higher-order corrections are observed, which increase the gluon-induced fraction from 53\% at LO to 64\% at NNLO.
L000279	\newline
L000280	
L000281	\textit{Conclusions---}\ignorespaces
L000282	In this letter, we compute the NNLO QCD corrections to identified hadron-in-jet production observables in 2-jet and 3-jet final states in $e^+e^-$ annihilation.
L000283	Our novel results establish the perturbative stability of the predictions, provided that the choice of the fragmentation scale takes into account the jet resolution, as advocated in~\cite{Dokshitzer:1987nm,Dokshitzer:1991wu,Procura:2009vm,Jain:2011xz,Kaufmann:2015hma}.
L000284	
L000285	Our calculation is performed in the \NNLOJET parton-level event generator framework, which allows to compute any infrared-safe observable derived from these final states, and to account for geometrical acceptance cuts that define the fiducial cross sections.
L000286	It shows that modern-day theory predictions no longer require ad hoc corrections to full geometrical acceptance for precision physics studies on $e^+e^-$ data.
L000287	
L000288	Our results demonstrate the increased sensitivity of the distribution of hadrons in the subleading-energy jets to the poorly constrained gluon-to-hadron fragmentation functions and show the impact of ALEPH hadron-in-jet data in their determination.
L000289	Our newly derived NNLO QCD corrections lay the ground for precision QCD studies on hadron-in-jet observables through the reanalysis of LEP data, following recent works on jets~\cite{Electron-PositronAlliance:2021kig} and event shapes~\cite{Electron-PositronAlliance:2025hze}, and at future high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders.
